newsitem.title: INDIA: India RBI stance seen holding rupee steady vs dlr.
newsitem.headline: India RBI stance seen holding rupee steady vs dlr.

text.p: The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)'s availability to buy dollars at 35.81/82 level is holding the rupee steady, dealers said on Friday.
Some dealers described it as a new strategy.
"They are there to buy at 35.82 even when the rupee is at 35.81," said a dealer at a Bombay bank, referring to RBI's recent interventions.
"There is no bargaining... they are a passive buyer," said the chief dealer at another bank.
Until the first week of June, RBI intervened only when the rupee threatened to jump the 35.80 per dollar barrier.
"The phase of reluctant intervention and obsession with repurcussions on money supply seem to be over," said a dealer.
The rupee was steady at 35.817/822 at Friday noon with no central bank intervention, dealers said.
Some dealers speculated that RBI's intervention seemed to be dictated by worries over a slowdown in India's export growth.
Many exporters blame the slowdown on an overvalued rupee.
